positions.commentary: The speaker admits that moving on from Amazon after it went from $10 to $14 was a very dumb mistake that got blown away.
The speaker mentions that Nick Sleep put all his money in Berkshire, Costco, and Amazon after shutting down his fund, and he outperformed anyone else.

thesis: This episode argues that Mohnish Pabrai regrets selling Amazon too early after it dropped to $10 in 2002, noting that holding such 'compounders' yields exceptional returns, while also highlighting that a peer (Nick Sleep) achieved superior performance by concentrating his portfolio in just three stocks: Berkshire Hathaway, Costco, and Amazon.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Amazon has performed exceptionally well since shutting down a fund that held it, and he regrets abandoning compounders like Amazon early.
claims.quote: And so I realized that, actually, I needed to go back to the engine, which is buying these great compounders, and I started to make my journey back.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Amazon stock collapsed to $10 a share in 2002, and he invested 10% of his fund in it at that price.
claims.quote: And at that time, Amazon stock had collapsed. It had collapsed down to $10 a share. And I was so impressed. And I put 10% of my fund at the time in Amazon at $10 a share.

claims.claim: The speaker admits that moving on from Amazon after it went from $10 to $14 was a very dumb mistake that got blown away.
claims.quote: And very quickly, it got to 14, and I moved on, okay? Very dumb, okay? There can't be things that are more dumber than that. And that's like a 330X that got blown away.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Nick Sleep put all his money in Berkshire, Costco, and Amazon after shutting down his fund, and he outperformed anyone else.
claims.quote: So when he shut down his fund, he had three stocks. He put all his money in, Berkshire, Costco, and Amazon. And I think he outperformed pretty much anyone else, no matter what they were doing.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions Coke and Amex as examples of businesses with long runways that Buffett had done well with, but does not mention Google.
claims.quote: businesses with these long runways and, you know, set it and forget it, type of thing, like what Buffett had done with Coke or Amex and so on.
